title: Non-minimality degree can be made arbitrarily large in an omega-categorical supersimple theory
author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
difficulty_reason: The fact asserts that for every n there is an omega-categorical supersimple theory with a type of non-minimality degree at least n (statement lines 1719-1723). The proof instantiates Evans's construction with a single k-ary relation, k = 3^{2n+1}, and the predimension delta(A) = 2|A| - |R(A)|/k!, verifying the two criteria on f(x) = log(x)/log(3) that make the generic theory simple (proof lines 1725-1733). The two steps that carry the content are then the n-transitivity computation, where an algebraic closure larger than n would have to be at least k in size and would violate the predimension bound through f, and the rank computation, which exhibits a k-element structure with exactly one instance of R to get SU(p) = 2 and hence the lower bound on the degree (proof lines 1733-1735). The construction is therefore explicit and the estimates are the substance. H2.
